songs.name: It's All Over Now Baby Blue

ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy Boston Garden ’82 with smoking Jerry, killer UJB→Playin' & Baby Blue
ai_show_review.review:
The September 18 1982 show at the Boston Garden is a quintessential early‑’80s Dead outing – the band rides a wave of raw excitement from the opening “Jack Straw” straight through to an emotional “It’s All Over Now, Baby Blue” encore. Jerry’s guitar is on fire all night, especially during the soaring Uncle John’s Band → Playing In The Band sequence and his vocal work shines on classics like “Jack Straw,” “Sugaree,” and the heartfelt “Baby Blue.” Brent Mydland’s piano adds a bright, melodic thrust that lifts the UJB>Playin' segue to new heights, while Phil delivers his usual sturdy low‑end with a few “Phil‑bomb” moments that keep the groove solid. Bob’s banter and dedication of “Samson & Delilah” to the Garden crowd injects that familiar Dead humor, and Bill (with Mickey) drives an energetic drum storm that, despite some thin‑ness on certain SBD mixes, propels the second set’s improvisations.

Across the five soundboard sources and two audience tapes, the consensus is clear: this night captures a band locked in, feeding off a raucous Boston crowd. Standout moments include the first Garden debut of “Throwing Stones,” an inspired “Samson & Delilah,” the seamless UJB → Playin' transition, and a warm, reflective “Baby Blue” that closes the evening on a high note. While some SBD mixes show the era‑typical thin highs or a toy‑like drum texture, the overall performance quality outweighs those quirks, making this concert a solid recommendation for any Deadhead looking to experience the early‑’80s groove.

best_recording.reason: Crisp, well‑balanced soundboard capture that preserves the band’s high energy and highlights the standout UJB→Playin' sequence while remaining a complete, full‑show recording.

key_highlights: Uncle John’s Band → Playing In The Band segue with Brent’s soaring piano
First Boston Garden appearance of “Throwing Stones” and a fiery “Samson & Delilah”
"It’s All Over Now, Baby Blue" encore that caps the night emotionally

band_performance.Jerry: Guitar is on fire all night – smoky tone, inventive solos, and strong vocal delivery on every major number.
band_performance.Phil: Solid bass foundation with a few standout “Phil‑bomb” moments (notably on “Samson & Delilah”), generally reliable though some reviewers note brief Phil‑lite spots.
band_performance.Bob: Charismatic banter and confident vocals, especially on the opener; dedicated "Samson" to the Garden building, adding his signature rapport.
band_performance.Keys: Brent Mydland’s piano shines, particularly during Uncle John’s Band → Playin' where he’s called “the man” for his melodic drive.
band_performance.Drums: Energetic dual‑drum work from Bill (and Mickey) fuels the high‑energy second set; drum solo praised despite occasional thin‑ness in certain SBD mixes.
